Harlem + Chocolate

Two good things that only get richer with time.

Dressed in gold

Harlem taught the world how to make an entrance.

Sunday best on Lenox. Gold lettering on a black awning. Chocolate got the same memo: wrap it in black, finish it in gold, and let it speak before the first bite.

Sweet on the block Sharing our love for Harlem + Chocolate

Every corner up here has a flavor memory. Chips and a cola from the bodega. Sweet potato pie at Grandma's table. Banana pudding after church. We fold those memories into ganache, so every bite tastes like somewhere you've been.

Stoop season Stoop season never ends uptown.

The stoop is where Harlem shares. So is a box of chocolate.

Brownstone steps have always been the neighborhood's living room: news traded, music playing, something sweet passed down the line. That's Strivers' Row on our wall, stoops and iron railings from floor to ceiling, so every box leaves the shop the way good things leave a stoop: shared.

From the homeland

Ghana's cocoa, Harlem's soul.

Harlem has deep West African roots, and so does chocolate. Ghana grows some of the finest cocoa on earth, and it's the heart of our Harlem to the Homeland bar. From there it gets painted, rolled and set in gold trays, uptown style.
